node.statement: Using validated nodes 1.4.1 and 1.4.2, the dyadic induction has a valid base and all root bounds are in scope: 1.4.2 gives a_1>=r_+, while 1.4.1 gives r_+/2>1/8>r_- and r_+>=1-C_diag e. If a_{2^k}>=r_+, node 1.3 gives a_{2^{k+1}}>=a_{2^k}/2>=r_+/2>r_-; nodes 1.2 and 1.4.1 give the dichotomy a_{2^{k+1}} in [0,r_-] union [r_+,infinity), so the lower branch is impossible and a_{2^{k+1}}>=r_+. Induction therefore gives a_{2^k}>=r_+ for every k>=0. Given n, choose k with 2^k>=n; the matrix-size monotonicity in node 1.3 yields a_n>=a_{2^k}>=r_+>=1-C_diag e, which is the claimed all-n lower-modulus conclusion.
